newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil softens on futures and slack demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil softens on futures and slack demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil weakened on Tuesday in line with softer benchmark futures and amid lacklustre demand, traders said. June IPE gas oil was $1.50 lower at $172.50 a tonne at 1200 GMT.
Heating oil barge premiums were assessed around June IPE +$1.0/$1.75 fob Rotterdam for first half June delivery.
There was talk that a barge had been done at $1.50 fob Rotterdam but this was not confirmed.
Low sulphur diesel remained under pressure as Algerian cargoes piled into the region despite a dearth of material in the Mediterranean.
Barge premiums were assessed at June IPE gas oil +$8.50/$9.0 fob Rotterdam for first half delivery and June IPE +$7.50 fob Antwerp.
Traders said the strength of the dollar was continuing to dog trade. At 1200 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.7227/34 against 1.7082/92 at the end of last week.
On the cargo front, traders said there was fair demand for low sulphur diesel into France where a major was looking for material.
Russian material was under pressure with premiums sinking to June IPE +0.75 cents/+$1.0 cif NWE.
